title: Capacity Commitment Surface and Surge Negotiation (Dedicated) PRD
creator: Aisha Malik
overview: Define a customer-facing product surface and backend orchestration for long-lived capacity commitments ("lease"), ephemeral surge capacity negotiation, and preemptive soft-burst rules for Dedicated tenants. Goal is to enable predictable throughput for committed workloads while providing safe, controllable transient burstability at predictable cost and isolation guarantees.
background: Customers ask for stronger guarantees around throughput and cost predictability for Dedicated pools while also wanting a way to handle short spikes without purchasing large permanent reservations. Current reserved pools give a flat reservation but we lack a compact UX and orchestration primitives for: (1) making short-term surge requests that do not permanently increase charges, (2) negotiating safety margins between tenants during contention, and (3) programmatic lease cancellation/reassignment with clear billing and eviction semantics.
goals: 1) Expose a Capacity Commitment API and Console flow for customers to create, modify, and cancel 'leases' (time-boxed reservations). 2) Build a Surge Negotiation protocol that allows a tenant to request ephemeral capacity (minutes-hours) with a firm acceptance or rejection and pricing estimate. 3) Implement tenant-side soft-burst policies and server-side arbitration that enforce isolation and graceful preemption. 4) Ship acceptance tests and rollout to a subset of Dedicated customers for beta.
non_goals: 1) Do not change core runtime kernel scheduling optimizations (this is orthogonal). 2) Not handling multi-cloud placement decisions in this iteration. 3) Not addressing on-prem install packaging; focus on Redwood-hosted Dedicated clusters.
success_metrics: - % of committed workload traffic served within 1x latency SLO for tenants with active lease >= 95% over 30d. - Number of ephemeral surge requests successfully served without requiring a permanent reservation. - Reduction in chargeback disputes related to unexpected preemption by 80% in pilot customers. - API adoption: 10 paying tenants using leases in first quarter post-launch.
user_personas: - Platform engineer at scale-up SaaS (primary): needs predictable p99 latency and predictable monthly spend. - Growth product manager (secondary): wants to enable burstable features during launches without long-term commitment. - SRE for enterprise (secondary): cares about isolation and clear evictability semantics.
user_stories: 1) As a platform engineer, I can create a 7-day lease of 250 vGPU-minutes that guarantees baseline throughput and will be billed as a time-boxed reservation. 2) As a product manager, I can request a 30-minute surge +20% capacity with an immediate price quote and fast acceptance to support a marketing push. 3) As an SRE, I can set a tenant soft-burst policy (max-burst-ratio, preemption-grace-seconds) to limit downstream impact when surge is revoked.
functional_requirements: FR-1: Lease object - API + Console that captures: tenant_id, capacity_units, start_time, end_time, cancellation_policy, billing_mode (prepay/postpay), SLA_tier. FR-2: Surge API - request_surges(tenant_id, delta_units, max_duration_minutes, max_price_per_unit) -> {accepted|rejected, accepted_duration, price}. FR-3: Soft-burst policy - per-tenant config (burst_ratio, max_concurrent_requests, preempt_priority, grace_window_seconds). FR-4: Arbitration service - evaluates competing surge requests using a priority-decay + safety-margin algorithm and returns deterministic outcomes. FR-5: Billing integration - lease and surge events produced to billing ledger with tags for waived-credits/discounts. FR-6: Audit logs - every lease/surge decision and eviction annotated for customer audit. FR-7: Observable metrics - per-lease throughput/latency, surge_accept_rate, surge_rejection_reasons, preemption_events.
non_functional_requirements: NFR-1: Lease API calls should complete within 300ms for create/read. NFR-2: Arbitration decisions for surge must be made within 1000ms during contention windows. NFR-3: Eviction signaling across runtime must have <5s median propagation. NFR-4: All actions must be GDPR-compliant and logged for 180 days in audit store. NFR-5: The feature must be togglable per-cluster via a feature-flag for staged rollout.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Create lease in Console and via API; verify billing ledger entry created with correct timeframe and capacity. AC-2: Simulate a spike and request a 15-minute surge; arbitration returns accepted and runtime serves the increased capacity; metrics show temporary increase and then ramp down. AC-3: Configure soft-burst policy and demonstrate eviction when higher-priority lease needs capacity; tenant receives eviction event with configured grace_window_seconds and partial fulfillment logs. AC-4: Arbitration must reject requests above configured safety margins and return explicit rejection codes that surface in Console. AC-5: Run end-to-end smoke test with a pilot tenant (QA harness) demonstrating SLA adherence and no silent failures for 7-day lease. AC-6: Security review sign-off (if required) and audit logs contain all events for the pilot cluster.
implementation_sketch: Phase 1: API + Console surface for Lease objects (CRUD) + Billing hooks. Phase 2: Basic Surge API and arbitration simulation in staging with a mock runtime. Phase 3: Runtime integration: preemptive signaling and eviction with grace windows. Phase 4: Observability, acceptance tests, and pilot rollout to 3 tenants. Core components: lease-service, surge-arbiter, scheduler-adapter (runtime bridge), billing-writer, audit-logger.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: feature-flagged on dedicated-staging clusters. 2) Select 3 existing Dedicated customers (low-risk) and enable API access for opt-in pilot. 3) Monitor for 14 days; iterate on pricing and rejection messaging. 4) Expand to Beta cohort (20 customers) and finalize UI text and billing docs. 5) GA release after meeting success metrics and operational readiness.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Dashboards: lease_count_by_tenant, active_surge_sessions, surge_accept_rate, preemption_rate. - Alerts: surge_arbitration_error_rate > 1% in 5m, eviction_signal_latency_P95 > 10s, billing_write_failures > 1 per minute. - On-call playbook: identify arbitration saturation, circuit-break to reject non-essential surge requests, and rollback feature flag per-cluster.
security_considerations: - Lease and surge API calls must require tenant-scoped auth tokens and RBAC to prevent cross-tenant manipulation. - Audit logs must be immutable and forwarded to customer-managed KMS if requested. - Pricing responses must avoid leaking internal capacity signals across tenants.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Option A (chosen): Lease + Surge as separate primitives with arbitration central service. Pros: clear billing/visibility, deterministic arbitration. Cons: more infra surface. Option B: Allow runtime to oversubscribe and rely on reactive throttling. Pros: simpler product. Cons: unpredictable billing and higher risk of noisy neighbor incidents. Option C: Long-term marketplace-style bidding for bursts. Deferred for later because it increases product complexity and legal/billing overhead.
open_questions: - Pricing model for surge: flat per-unit premium vs. time-weighted auction? Recommendation: start with fixed premium + capped acceptance rate. - Cancellation refunds: what prorate granularity is acceptable for customers? - Will enterprises require signed amendments to the lease that affect legal billing? Engage Legal. - Should we expose predictive recommendations for when to buy a lease? Consider in later iteration.
qa_testing_plan: - Unit tests for lease CRUD and billing ledger events. - Integration tests: surge arbitration simulation and runtime eviction hooks in staging. - Chaos tests: simultaneous surge floods from 10 tenants to validate arbitration stability. - Pilot acceptance tests with tenants: p99 latency under lease and under surge scenarios.
operational_runbook: - How to identify stuck leases and manually revoke. - How to clear surge backlogs and force-fail arbitrator in emergency. - How to reconcile billing disputes: tools to replay arbitration events and audit log. - On-call steps to roll back feature flag for a cluster.
documentation_and_customer_communication: - Console help doc: 'Capacity Commitments and Surge Requests' walk-through. - API reference for Lease and Surge endpoints with examples. - Billing FAQ: surge pricing, refunds, and SLA credits. - Email templates for pilot on-boarding and incident notifications.
notes: Keep UX minimal for alpha: create lease wizard, one-step surge request modal, and clear status indicators for acceptance/rejection. Iterate pricing conservatively to avoid customer shock.
